headline: Grim FC bench-boosts to 87 and stretches the lead to 24
summary: Louis Grimoldby was Manager of the Week with 87 points as Grim FC’s Bench Boost, Haaland captaincy and 15-point Neto differential powered him clear at the top. Mark Horton moves into second on 501, but Will Finney is only 6 points back and fourth-placed olly barnes is just 3 behind him, with Tim Chodha level on 492.
report:
Louis Grimoldby is setting the early pace in the Biddenham Fantasy League. Grim FC’s 87 was the gameweek’s top score, comfortably above the 65.6 league average and 56 global average, and it takes the leader to 525 overall. With 31 gameweeks remaining, Mark Horton is now the closest challenger on 501, 24 points back — but the chasing pack is tightly packed behind him.

Grimoldby’s Bench Boost was impeccably timed, with no transfer hits to spoil the total. Haaland was the obvious captaincy call for 23 of 26 managers and returned 13 points; Louis was among them, doubling the haul. The real separator was Neto: owned by Louis alone, the CHE player delivered 15 points to make this a properly punchy week. Louis is also the league’s hottest manager over the last three gameweeks with 214 net points, so this is looking less like a one-week spike and more like form.

Behind him, Mark Horton climbed one place into second after scoring 69, while Will Finney’s 75 moved 0v3rf1tt3d.h5 up two places to third on 495. There is only 6 points between Horton and Finney, then just 3 between Finney and olly barnes in fourth. Grasshoppers scored 66 to reach 492, exactly level with Tim Chodha’s Hakuna Juan Mata, whose 59-point week saw him fall three places to fifth. The podium may have some breathing room at the very top, but the queue beneath it is shoulder-to-shoulder.

James Geary was the nearest thing to Grim FC’s 87, posting 85 with the Triple Captain active, while David Tonks hit 82 after playing a Wildcard. George Foy’s Triple Captain produced 75, Chris Beeden’s Bench Boost returned 72, and Abi Speight’s Triple Captain brought in 64. Six chips were fired in one gameweek — an early-season barrage — while 17 Triple Captains, 16 Bench Boosts and 19 Free Hits remain in reserve.

The differentials did plenty of damage. James Marshall had Evanilson’s 12-point return and shared Tavernier’s 10 points with olly barnes. Chris Beeden and Abi Speight both benefited from Kostoulas’s 12, while David Tonks found Manzambi for 11 and Dan Birkinshaw had the league’s only Foden for 9. At the more popular end, Haaland’s 13 rewarded 88.5% ownership, while João Pedro and Rogers returned only 2 apiece for their many backers.

The captaincy horror show belonged to Jamie Mitchell, whose Cherki armband brought a brutal 0. Jamie scored 36 overall and tumbled 8 places, the biggest fall of the week. Georg Coakley fared even worse on points, collecting the wooden spoon with 35 and dropping 5 places; Georgingham Unai-ted is also the league’s coldest side over the last three gameweeks on 136. Spare a thought, too, for Paul Alexis, who left 19 points on the bench.

Elsewhere, Alan Eckett-Brown was the week’s biggest climber, rising 6 places after a 72-point return. James Geary gained 5 places and David Tonks 4, both riding their big scores upwards. The season’s single-game benchmark remains Mark Horton’s 116 from Gameweek 2, but Louis Grimoldby has made the latest statement: 87 points, a Bench Boost deployed, and a 24-point lead to defend.
